skin.setting: a Scottish distillery snowbound at Hogmanay, 1949
skin.title: A Dram Before Dying
skin.styleGuide: A moody mid-century Scottish gothic aesthetic with heavy shadows, snowdrifts against granite stonework, copper pot stills, woollen tweeds, and lantern light cutting through the winter chill.

rooms.name: the distillery yard
rooms.description: The open cobblestone yard, blanketed in deep snowdrifts under the howling mountain blizzard.

rooms.name: the malt kiln
rooms.description: A soot-stained drying floor smelling richly of burning peat and roasted barley.

rooms.name: the mash house
rooms.description: The warm, steam-filled chamber housing the massive cast-iron mash tun.

rooms.name: the manager's office
rooms.description: A wood-panelled office cluttered with ledgers, sample flasks, and a glowing coal grate.

rooms.name: the tun room
rooms.description: The cavernous hall lined with towering wooden washbacks bubbling with fermenting wort.

rooms.name: the still house
rooms.description: The heart of the distillery, filled with the gleam of giant copper swan-neck stills.

rooms.name: the cooperage
rooms.description: A draughty workshop littered with oak staves, iron hoops, and shavings of seasoned wood.

rooms.name: the bonded warehouse
rooms.description: A dark earthen-floored cellar stacked high with slumbering sherry and bourbon casks.

people.name: Hamish Boyd
people.bio: Hamish has tended the mash tuns for thirty hard winters. He believes the distillery's secret recipe was stolen from his own grandfather.
people.voice: A gruff, rumbling Highland baritone with an abrupt manner.
people.motive: Archie planned to replace traditional mashing methods and dismiss Hamish without a pension.
people.portrait: A burly, weathered man in his late fifties with bushy grey eyebrows, thick mutton chops, wearing a coarse woollen waistcoat and rolled-up twill shirt.

people.name: Fiona MacLeod
people.bio: Sharp-eyed and meticulous, Fiona has managed the estate accounts since the end of the war. She knows every secret tucked into the distillery's financial registers.
people.voice: Crisp, precise, and measured, with an educated Lowland cadence.
people.motive: Archie discovered significant discrepancies in the accounts and threatened her with prison.
people.portrait: A slender woman in her thirties with dark hair swept back in a neat victory roll, wearing wire-rimmed spectacles and a tailored tweed skirt suit.

people.name: Callum Grant
people.bio: A quiet veteran trying to rebuild his life amidst the fires of the still house. He has long endured the bitter temper of his superiors.
people.voice: Soft-spoken, hesitant, and carrying a quiet nervous tremor.
people.motive: Archie repeatedly humiliated him and threatened to ruin his reputation across the whisky trade.
people.portrait: A gaunt young man in his late twenties with haunted eyes, dark ruffled hair, and a heavy knitted fisherman's jumper.

people.name: Isla Sinclair
people.bio: Isla tests each distillation run with scientific precision in her makeshift laboratory. She views the romantic lore of whisky making with sheer pragmatism.
people.voice: Clinical, cool, and articulate, choosing every word deliberately.
people.motive: Archie denied her rightful patent credit for an innovative blending process and took the royalties himself.
people.portrait: An imposing woman in her forties with ash-blonde hair pinned into a severe bun, sharp cheekbones, wearing a dark woollen cardigan over a high-collared blouse.

people.name: Donald Ross
people.bio: Donald shapes the oak casks that give Balmoral malt its prized character. He is fierce in defending the integrity of his craft.
people.voice: Loud, hearty, and thick with an Aberdeenshire drawl.
people.motive: Archie signed an order for cheap second-rate barrels, mocking Donald's insistence on master craft.
people.portrait: A stocky, broad-shouldered man in his fifties with ruddy skin, a thick salt-and-pepper beard, and a heavy flannel shirt.

people.name: Morag Campbell
people.bio: The government revenue officer assigned to monitor every drop of proof spirit produced on site. Her uncompromising inspection tours are dreaded by staff and owners alike.
people.voice: Stern, authoritative, and completely unimpressed by excuses.
people.motive: Archie attempted to blacken her official record to prevent her from exposing his illicit untaxed sales.
people.portrait: A formidable woman in her late forties with steely grey hair cut short, upright military posture, wearing a dark double-breasted officer-cut overcoat.

people.name: Archie MacNair
people.bio: The wealthy and domineering owner of Balmoral Crag Distillery. His tyrannical management made him enemies among everyone under his roof.
people.portrait: A stern, silver-haired man in his sixties with a thin moustache, arrogant bearing, dressed in an expensive three-piece tweed suit.

silence: Hamish scowls and shakes his head. 'I've nothing more to say to you on that.'
Fiona adjusts her glasses. 'My records show nothing regarding that matter.'
Callum shifts uncomfortably. 'I don't know anything about that, truly.'
Isla looks up coldly. 'I have no relevant observations to share.'
Donald shrugs his broad shoulders. 'Cannot help you there, Inspector.'
Morag replies curtly. 'I noted nothing of significance regarding that.'
Archie MacNair offers only the cold silence of the grave.
skin.briefing: On Hogmanay night of 1949, a ferocious blizzard severed all mountain passes leading to the Balmoral Crag Distillery, trapping the staff and owner inside. Shortly before the bells of the New Year could ring, the proprietor Archie MacNair was found dead in the still house. With the snow cutting off all outside assistance, you must sift through physical evidence and testimonies to piece together the hours leading to MacNair's demise and identify the killer.
skin.scene: A snowbound Scottish stone distillery under moonlight, with drifts piled high against granite walls, glowing amber windows, and a tall brick chimney venting peat smoke into a blizzard.
skin.summingUp:
The winter chill has settled deep into the granite stonework tonight, and by the heavy copper pot stills, Archie MacNair drew his last breath. We can trace the truth through the shadows. To begin with, the murder was not at five o'clock or midnight, because Card 7 narrows down when the murder happened. Furthermore, the murder was not at eleven o'clock, because Card 14 says a room held nobody. Nor could it have taken place at ten o'clock, because the killer and Archie MacNair were both in the still house when it happened.

That same fact dictates our suspects: Hamish Boyd is in the clear, because the killer and Archie MacNair were both in the still house when it happened. Next, Donald Ross is in the clear, because supposing it was Donald Ross leaves nothing that fits. Similarly, Morag Campbell is in the clear, because supposing it was Morag Campbell leaves nothing that fits. The hours narrow relentlessly under the lantern light: the murder was not at six o'clock, because supposing the murder happened at six o'clock leaves nothing that fits; the murder was not at seven o'clock, because supposing the murder happened at seven o'clock leaves nothing that fits; and the murder was not at eight o'clock, because supposing the murder happened at eight o'clock leaves nothing that fits.

That leaves nine o'clock as the fatal hour in the still house. As for who stood there in the cold: Callum Grant is in the clear, because Fiona MacLeod and Isla Sinclair cannot both have been innocent. And lastly, Fiona MacLeod is in the clear, because there is no way for Isla Sinclair to have been innocent. Archie denied you your rightful patent credit for an innovative blending process and took the royalties himself, and at nine o'clock in the still house, Isla Sinclair, you took his life.
